claims.claim: Shuter and colleagues argued that size-dependent winter starvation alone can explain the northern range limits of smallmouth bass, yellow perch and Eurasian perch (Shuter et al. 1980; Shuter & Post 1990; both abstracts)
claims.note: full text not obtained, and no abstract found in Crossref. Lead from another reader: the Shuter et al. 1980 abstract covers smallmouth only, so the perch part of this sentence rests on Shuter & Post 1990 alone and is unverified

claims.claim: Shuter & Post's smallmouth respiration RA: FB4 stores 0.03, Mille Lacs used 0.009, suggesting a unit error
claims.note: the published value could not be read. Ahrenstorff & Holbrook 2016 (Table 1, read in this batch) do apply RA 0.009 with RB −0.21, RQ 3.3, RTO 30, RTM 37, ACT 2, SDA 0.16, CA 0.25, CB −0.31, CQ 3.8, CTO 29, CTM 36, FA 0.104, UA 0.068 and credit them to Shuter & Post 1990 — the comparison the rewrite needs is FB4's stored row against Shuter & Post's own table

claims.claim: fish die after losing roughly 35–45 % of their mass; the basis of size-selective overwinter mortality (Shuter & Post 1990)

notes: Blocked; tier 1, so worth the human's library fetch: doi:10.1577/1548-8659(1990)119<0314:CPVATZ>2.3.CO;2 (TAFS 119(2): 314–336). When read, check: (1) which species the range-limit argument covers (smallmouth bass, yellow perch, Eurasian perch?) and whether it claims winter starvation 'alone' explains the limits; (2) the smallmouth bioenergetics parameters as printed, especially RA and its units (FB4 stores 0.03; Mille Lacs used 0.009) and whether consumption/respiration are in g g⁻¹ d⁻¹ or J; (3) any starvation-endurance figure (the config's 35–45 % mass loss) and the size thresholds for first-winter survival that §3.6.8 and Table 3.6-9 use via Dudley & Trial 2014.
